Inspect the request and repository.
Ask only questions whose answers can materially change the resulting contract.

strategy.hypothesis: Defining materiality in terms of observable behavior or authorized scope will reduce questions that elicit incidental implementation details and later turn them into contract clauses, while preserving questions needed to resolve genuine behavioral ambiguity.
strategy.target_selection: Select the exact baseline sentence `Ask only questions whose answers can materially change the resulting contract.` and replace only it with `Ask only questions whose answers can change an observable outcome or the authorized scope of the resulting contract.`

strategy.hypothesis: Removing repository inspection as an unconditional interview instruction will reduce the conversion of incidental repository artifacts into requirements, while the remaining request-focused instructions preserve the skill's core clarification behavior.
strategy.target_selection: Select the exact baseline sentence `Inspect the request and repository.` and delete only that sentence.

strategy.hypothesis: Explicitly excluding unrequested exhaustive examples will reduce acceptance contracts that enumerate every inferred compatibility consequence, without weakening requested observable outcomes or explicitly answered requirements.
strategy.target_selection: Select the exact baseline sentence `State contract clauses as observable outcomes, and omit specific implementation or validation mechanisms unless the request or an explicit interview answer requires that mechanism.` and add immediately after it exactly this sentence: `Do not promote inferred edge cases or exhaustive examples into separate requirements unless explicitly requested or answered.`
